question: How many polynomials of the form \(x^5 + ax^4 + bx^3 + cx^2 + dx\) \(+ 2020,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) and \(d\) are real numbers, have the property that whenever \(r\) is a root, so is \(\dfrac{-1 + i\sqrt3}{2}\cdot r?\) (Note that \(i = \sqrt{-1}.\))
solution:
The given multiplier has cube equal to \(1\), so it groups nonzero roots into triples. A degree-\(5\) polynomial can contain only one such triple, making repeated roots essential.

Write
\[
\omega=\frac{-1+i\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
Direct calculation gives
\[
\omega^2=\frac{-1-i\sqrt3}{2},\qquad
\omega^3=1,\qquad \omega+\omega^2=-1.
\]
Let \(P\) be a polynomial satisfying the conditions. Since \(P(0)=2020\), none of its roots is zero. Starting with any root \(z\), the stated property produces the three distinct roots
\[
z,\quad \omega z,\quad \omega^2z.
\]
Any root outside this triple would generate another disjoint triple: if the triples shared a member, multiplication by a suitable power of \(\omega\) would show that they were the same triple. Six distinct roots are impossible for a degree-\(5\) polynomial. Thus \(P\) has exactly three distinct roots.

Real coefficients imply \(P(\overline z)=\overline{P(z)}\), so nonreal roots occur in conjugate pairs. Among three distinct roots, at least one must therefore be real; call it \(r\). The root set is
\[
\{r,r\omega,r\omega^2\}.
\]
The last two roots are conjugates and have equal multiplicities, since conjugating the factorization leaves \(P\) unchanged.

A degree-\(5\) polynomial has five complex roots counted with multiplicity. If \(r\) has multiplicity \(m\), and each nonreal root has multiplicity \(k\), then
\[
m+2k=5,\qquad m,k\ge1.
\]
The only possibilities are
\[
(m,k)=(3,1)\quad\text{or}\quad(1,2).
\]
The product of all five roots is
\[
r^m(r\omega)^k(r\omega^2)^k=r^5,
\]
since \(\omega^{3k}=1\). For a monic quintic, its constant term is the negative of that product. Consequently
\[
r^5=-2020,
\]
which fixes the unique real value \(r=-\sqrt[5]{2020}\).

Both multiplicity patterns actually work. Using
\[
(x-r\omega)(x-r\omega^2)=x^2+rx+r^2,
\]
they give
\[
(x-r)^3(x^2+rx+r^2)
\quad\text{and}\quad
(x-r)(x^2+rx+r^2)^2.
\]
These are distinct monic quintics with real coefficients, constant term \(-r^5=2020\), and the required root triple. Hence there are exactly \(\boxed{2}\) polynomials, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
